content: Flurandrenolide is a medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as itching, redness, dryness, crusting, scaling, inflammation, and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It may also be used for other purposes as directed by your doctor or pharmacist. Flurandrenolide is available in different forms, including ointment, cream, lotion, and medicated tape, for application to the skin. Typically, it is applied two or three times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not apply more or less than prescribed, and do not use it more frequently than instructed. Avoid applying it to other areas of your body or covering the treated area with wraps or bandages unless specifically directed by your doctor. Before applying the medication, wash or soak the affected area thoroughly unless doing so irritates your skin. Apply a thin layer of the ointment, cream, or lotion sparingly and rub it in gently. If using the lotion on your scalp, part your hair, apply a small amount to the affected area, and rub it in gently. Protect the area from washing or rubbing until the lotion dries. You may wash your hair as usual, but not immediately after applying the medication. Avoid prolonged use on the face, genital and rectal areas, skin folds, or armpits unless directed by your doctor. If applying the medication to your face, ensure it does not come into contact with your eyes. If using it on a child’s diaper area, avoid tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as these may increase side effects. Do not apply cosmetics or other skin preparations to the treated area without consulting your doctor. If your doctor prescribes flurandrenolide tape, follow these steps and any accompanying special instructions: Clean the affected area gently with germicidal soap (ask your pharmacist for recommendations) and water, removing any scales or crusts. Dry your skin thoroughly. Shave or clip the hair in the area to ensure the tape adheres well and can be removed comfortably. Cut a piece of tape slightly larger than the treatment area, rounding off the corners. Remove the white paper backing to expose the medicated surface, ensuring the tape does not stick to itself. Smooth your skin and press the tape into place. Replace the tape as directed on your prescription label, usually every 12 hours. Remove the old tape, wash your skin, and allow the area to dry for one hour before applying fresh tape. If the ends of the tape loosen before it is time to replace it, trim the ends and replace them with new tape. If your doctor instructs you to wrap or bandage the treated area, follow these steps: Soak the area in water or wash it thoroughly. While the skin is moist, gently rub the medication into the affected areas. Cover the area with plastic wrap (e.g., Saran Wrap or Handi-Wrap). Secure the plastic with gauze, an elastic bandage, or adhesive tape on the normal skin adjacent to the treated area. Alternatively, plastic gloves may be used for hands, plastic bags for feet, or a shower cap for the scalp. Seal the edges of the plastic wrap carefully to ensure it adheres closely to the skin. If the area is moist, leave the edges partially unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. Leave the plastic wrap in place as directed by your doctor, usually no more than 12 hours per day. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time a new plastic wrapping is applied. Do not discontinue treatment abruptly without consulting your doctor. Before using flurandrenolide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to flurandrenolide or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially cancer chemotherapy agents, other topical medications, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have an infection or a history of diabetes, glaucoma, cataracts, circulation disorders, or immune disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using flurandrenolide, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Flurandrenolide may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Drying or cracking of the skin Acne Itching Changes in skin color If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Severe skin rash Difficulty breathing or swallowing Wheezing Signs of a skin infection, such as redness, swelling, or oozing pus If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature and do not allow it to freeze. Dispose of any outdated or unused medication properly, and do not use it to treat other skin conditions. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist.
